title: Problem Overview and References
content: Erdős Problem #802 asks whether $K_r$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ must contain an independent set of size $\gg_r (\log t / t) \cdot n$. This is the AEKS conjecture (Ajtai-Erdős-Komlós-Szemerédi, 1981). The header documents the resolution timeline: AKS (1980) proved the full bound for $r = 3$ (triangle-free graphs), AEKS (1981) proved a weaker $(\log\log t / t) \cdot n$ bound for general $r$, Shearer (1995) improved to $(\log t / (\log\log t \cdot t)) \cdot n$, and Alon (1996) proved the full bound under stronger local sparsity assumptions.
mathContext: $\alpha(G) \geq c_r \cdot \frac{\log t}{t} \cdot n$ for $K_r$-free graphs with average degree $t$

title: Imports and Namespace
content: Imports Mathlib's simple graph and clique infrastructure, natural number and real number arithmetic, and the natural logarithm from `Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic`. The `open SimpleGraph Real` brings graph notation and `Real.log` into scope.
mathContext: Uses `SimpleGraph.IsClique` for clique detection, `Real.log` for $\ln$, and `Fintype.card` for $|V|$

title: Graph Basics: Average Degree and Clique-Freeness
content: Defines `numVertices`, `avgDegree` ($\bar{d}(G) = 2|E|/|V|$), `IsCliqueFree G r` (no $r$-clique exists), and `IsTriangleFree` ($K_3$-free). The average degree $t$ is the key parameter: denser graphs have larger $t$, and the conjecture asserts that forbidding $K_r$ forces independent sets of size $\Omega((\log t / t) \cdot n)$. The triangle-free case ($r = 3$) is singled out because it was solved first and has the strongest connections to Ramsey theory.
mathContext: $\bar{d}(G) = \frac{2|E(G)|}{|V(G)|}$; $G$ is $K_r$-free $\iff \forall S \subseteq V,\; |S| = r \Rightarrow S$ is not a clique

title: Independent Set and Independence Number
content: `IsIndependent G s` states that no two distinct vertices in $s$ are adjacent. The independence number $\alpha(G) = \sup\{|S| : S \text{ independent in } G\}$ is the size of the largest independent set. Computing $\alpha(G)$ is NP-hard in general, but structural conditions like $K_r$-freeness provide lower bounds. The AEKS conjecture gives a lower bound in terms of average degree.
mathContext: $\alpha(G) = \max\{|S| : S \subseteq V,\; \forall u, v \in S,\; u \neq v \Rightarrow u \not\sim v\}$

title: The AEKS Conjecture
content: The formal conjecture `AEKSConjecture r` states: there exists $c > 0$ such that every $K_r$-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and average degree $t \geq 2$ satisfies $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot (\log t / t) \cdot n$. The bound $(\log t / t) \cdot n$ is optimal: random $K_r$-free graphs (constructed via the probabilistic method or algebraic constructions) achieve this bound up to constant factors. The helper function `aeksBound` computes the target value.
mathContext: $\text{AEKS}_r: \exists c_r > 0,\; \forall G \text{ } K_r\text{-free with } \bar{d}(G) = t \geq 2:\; \alpha(G) \geq c_r \cdot \frac{\log t}{t} \cdot n$

title: AEKS (1981): First Bound with Double Logarithm
content: Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi (1981) proved $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot (\log\log(t+1) / t) \cdot n$ for $K_r$-free graphs. This was the first bound showing that forbidding $K_r$ forces independence numbers significantly larger than the trivial $n/t$ (which follows from the greedy algorithm). The double-logarithm factor ($\log\log t$ vs $\log t$) left a gap that would take 14 years to close.
mathContext: $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log\log(t+1)}{t} \cdot n$ for $K_r$-free $G$ with average degree $t$

title: Shearer (1995): Improved Bound
content: Shearer (1995) improved the general bound to $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1) \cdot t} \cdot n$. This is the best known bound for general $r$: it has the correct $\log t$ in the numerator but retains an extra $\log\log t$ factor in the denominator. The proof uses a refined probabilistic argument with entropy-based analysis of random independent sets.
mathContext: $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1) \cdot t} \cdot n$ for $K_r$-free $G$; best known for $r \geq 4$

title: AKS (1980): Triangle-Free Case Solved
content: Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi (1980) proved the full conjectured bound $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot (\log t / t) \cdot n$ for triangle-free graphs ($r = 3$). This was actually proved *before* the general conjecture was formally stated. The proof pioneered the use of the semi-random method in combinatorics. The derived theorem `conjecture_true_for_r3` shows that `AEKSConjecture 3` follows directly, with the proof simply unwrapping the triangle-free definition.
mathContext: $G$ triangle-free with $\bar{d}(G) = t \Rightarrow \alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log t}{t} \cdot n$; this proves $\text{AEKS}_3$

title: Alon's Local Chromatic Version (1996)
content: Alon (1996) proved the full $(\log t / t) \cdot n$ bound under the stronger assumption that $G$ is *locally $(r-2)$-chromatic*: every neighborhood $N(v)$ has chromatic number $\leq r-2$. This is stronger than $K_r$-free (since $K_r$-free implies $N(v)$ is $K_{r-1}$-free, not necessarily $(r-2)$-colorable). The formalization includes `IsLocallyChromatic` (simplified as a placeholder) and the axiom `locally_chromatic_implies_clique_free` relating the two conditions.
mathContext: $\chi(G[N(v)]) \leq r-2$ for all $v$ $\Rightarrow$ $\alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log t}{t} \cdot n$; note $K_r$-free $\not\Rightarrow$ locally $(r-2)$-chromatic

title: Ramsey Theory Connection
content: The AKS triangle-free independence bound directly implies the Ramsey lower bound $R(3, k) \geq c \cdot k^2 / \log k$. The argument: if $G$ is a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with no independent set of size $k$, then $n < R(3, k)$. By contrapositive, the AKS bound gives $k \leq \alpha(G) \leq c \cdot (\log t / t) \cdot n$, and maximizing $n$ yields the Ramsey bound. A separate axiom states the classical bound $\alpha(G) \geq c\sqrt{n \log n}$ for triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices.
mathContext: $R(3, k) \geq c \cdot k^2 / \log k$; also $\alpha(G) \geq c\sqrt{n \log n}$ for triangle-free $G$ on $n$ vertices

title: Main Result: erdos_802
content: The main theorem `erdos_802` packages two results as a conjunction: (1) $\text{AEKS}_3$ (the full conjecture for $r = 3$, proved via AKS 1980), and (2) Shearer's partial bound for all $r \geq 3$. The proof constructs the pair by calling `conjecture_true_for_r3` for the first component and `shearer_1995` for the second. The file also includes string-valued status and answer summaries, and `#check` commands for verification.
mathContext: $\text{AEKS}_3 \wedge (\forall r \geq 3,\; \alpha(G) \geq c \cdot \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1) \cdot t} \cdot n \text{ for } K_r\text{-free } G)$
